questions.q: After selling approximately 979 shares of ZQX to hedge the portfolio, what happens to the portfolio's gamma and vega?
options: Both gamma and vega are also flattened to zero by the stock hedge
Gamma and vega remain completely unchanged, because a share of stock has zero gamma and zero vega
Gamma increases while vega decreases
Both gamma and vega become negative
questions.explain: A delta-hedge only offsets delta. Shares of stock have zero gamma and zero vega, so hedging with shares leaves the portfolio's gamma (+17.7) and vega (+$163 per vol point) completely untouched.

questions.q: Why does the delta-hedge need to be rebalanced if ZQX's price moves after the hedge is put on?
options: Because the risk-free rate changes every time the stock price moves
Because nonzero gamma means every option's delta shifts as the price moves, while the stock hedge's delta stays fixed at 1 per share, so net delta drifts away from zero again
Because Black-Scholes prices become invalid once a trade is executed
Because contract multipliers change over time
questions.explain: Gamma measures how delta changes as the underlying price moves. Since the hedge is sized once based on the delta at one point in time, any subsequent price move shifts the options' deltas and reopens the gap, requiring the hedge to be recalculated.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does it mean that the hedge 'worked'?
options: It eliminated all risk in the portfolio permanently
It flattened the portfolio's net delta, offsetting small directional moves — nothing more and nothing less
It guaranteed a profit regardless of market conditions
It eliminated the need for any further risk management
questions.explain: A delta-hedge accomplishes exactly what it's designed for: offsetting small directional exposure. It does not address gamma, vega, or any other residual risk.

questions.q: Which of the following should a strong presentation of this capstone project include, according to the lesson?
options: Only the final hedge share count, with no other detail
A claim that the hedge eliminates all risk in the portfolio
The pricing code, a results table of per-option and portfolio Greeks, the hedge calculation, and an honest summary of what remains exposed
A guarantee of a specific investment return to any reader
questions.explain: A strong presentation shows the actual code, the computed results, the hedge trade, and is explicit about its limitations — naming residual gamma and vega exposure rather than overstating what was accomplished.

questions.q: Which Black-Scholes assumption is explicitly named in this lesson as a simplification a real trading desk has to work around?
options: That interest rates are always negative
That volatility is constant, when in reality it changes over time
That stock prices can only move in whole-dollar increments
That options can only be exercised on the day they are purchased
questions.explain: Black-Scholes assumes constant volatility (along with no transaction costs, continuous trading, and lognormal returns), which real trading desks must account for and work around in practice.
